class.name: ArrayCellMeshND
class.description: ArrayCellMeshND is a class for specifying cell meshes with arrays of data, including the vertices and cells. Unlike the specialized [CellMeshND] classes such as [BoxPolyMeshND], ArrayCellMeshND can store any cell mesh, allowing users to create custom meshes with arbitrary data.

method.name: append_vertex
method.description: Append a vertex to the cell mesh. If [param deduplicate_vertices] is [code]true[/code], the method will check if the vertex already exists in the [member vertex_positions] array and return the index of the existing vertex. If the vertex does not exist, it will be appended to the vertices array and its index will be returned. In both cases, the returned index points to a vertex identical to the input vertex.

method.name: merge_with
method.description: Merges the current cell mesh with another cell mesh, copying the contents of [param other] into this cell mesh with a relative transform of [param transform]. If only one of the meshes has normals, the other normals will be initialized to zero.

members.member: The dimension of the mesh, defined by the number of components in the first vertex position. Setting this resizes the first position to the new dimension, truncating or padding it with zeros as necessary. Other positions are truncated if too long, but shorter and empty positions remain compact. Setting this on a mesh without vertices does not create a vertex, so its dimension remains zero. Changing the dimension clears simplex cell indices, boundary normals, vertex normals, and texture mapping, because the number of vertices per simplex cell changes. Setting the same dimension preserves the cells and truncates overlong attribute vectors without expanding compact or empty entries.

The boundary normals of the simplex cells. Boundary normals define which side of the cell is the front side, and therefore should be drawn. Boundary normals can also be used to calculate vertex normals to determine how lighting angles are calculated for the cell. Each VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]) in this array is for one cell, and should be normalized. This array should either be one-Nth as long as the [member simplex_cell_vertex_indices] array, or empty for no normals, or else the mesh is invalid. Each normal may have at most N components. Missing trailing components are treated as zero.

The texture coordinate mapping of the simplex cells. Each VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]) in this array is the texture space mapping for one vertex instance in a simplex cell, meaning [method CellMeshND.get_indices_per_simplex_cell] per cell. This array should either be the same length as the [member simplex_cell_vertex_indices] array, or empty for no texture coordinate mapping, or else the mesh is invalid. For an N-dimensional mesh, each texture coordinate may have at most N-1 components. Missing trailing components are treated as zero.

The vertex indices of the simplex cells. For an N-dimensional mesh, every N integers defines a simplex cell (as returned by [method CellMeshND.get_indices_per_simplex_cell]), for a total of [method CellMeshND.get_simplex_cell_count] cells. Each integer is an index to the [member vertex_positions] array. Integers in this array should not exceed the length of the vertices array, or else the mesh is invalid.

The normals of the vertex indices of simplex cells. Vertex normals define how lighting angles are calculated for the cell. Each VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]) in this array is for one vertex instance in a simplex cell, meaning N per cell, and each should be normalized. This array should either be the same length as the [member simplex_cell_vertex_indices] array, or empty for no normals, or else the mesh is invalid. Each normal may have at most N components. Missing trailing components are treated as zero.

The vertices of the cell mesh. Each vertex is a VectorN ([PackedFloat64Array]). The first position defines the mesh dimension; subsequent positions may omit trailing zero components, but must not exceed that dimension. Indices of cells and edges refer to the items in this array. The vertices array must be kept consistent with the cell indices array, such that each cell index points to a valid vertex index, or else the mesh is invalid.
